newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Vienna to sell all Bank Austria stake.
newsitem.headline: Vienna to sell all Bank Austria stake.

text.p: Vienna's ruling coalition of Social Democrats and conservative People's Party said on Tuesday it had agreed to sell the city's entire 49 percent stake in market leader Bank Austria within six years.
At a joint news conference Social Democrat mayor Michael Haeupl and his conservative deputy Bernhard Goerg said the two parties would make a joint proposal at a council meeting later on Tuesday.
"By the end of 1997 an international investment house will present a scheme for the sale, taking into account the need for an Austrian solution. A six-year timetable is foreseen," the motion said.

The City of Vienna indirectly owns around 44 percent of Bank Austria voting shares through its AVZ holding company, Goerg said. The remaining Vienna shares, which would also be sold off, are with a second holding company, Wiener Holding.
The city would seek buyers for its AVZ stake, valued at 25-35 billion schillings, among institutional investors, strategic partners and over the stock market.
"The privatisation must ensure that a majority Austrian interest remains and there is no significant decline in the share price," the proposal said.
After the sale, the City of Vienna would cease to act as guarantor for Bank Austria, which has a triple A credit rating. Haeupl ruled out a deterioration in the bank's rating.
"I don't believe there will be a negative impact," he said.
Revenue from the sale would flow into Vienna coffers "without any tax burden to the community", the proposal said.
Haeupl and Goerg declined to say which investment house was likely to advise in the sale. -- Vienna newsroom, +43-1 531 12 254
